summary: Correct, minimal fix: computes trailing-punctuation count on the unescaped string and slices that many characters off the end of the escaped `middle`, fixing the index mismatch between escaped and unescaped lengths that produced the duplicated `lt` in the trail. Matches the issue's expected output and is the natural general fix.

issues.description: Slicing `punctuation_count` chars off the escaped `middle` assumes each trailing punctuation char in the unescaped form maps to exactly one char in the escaped form. Fails if a trailing TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS char is itself a multi-char entity (e.g. `.`/`!`), where one unescaped punctuation char corresponds to multiple escaped chars. This is a pre-existing limitation (original code mishandled it too), an extreme edge case, and not a regression introduced by this patch.
